tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

content.content:
# Tools that withhold what the app saw: findings to confirm

Written 2026-11-01 for an agent who has not seen the session that produced it. Please try to prove each finding wrong. Every finding comes from reading the code. **Nothing here has been run or reproduced, and nothing has been fixed.**

## The question

JusPrin is a desktop 3D-printing slicer forked from OrcaSlicer. An AI model chats with people and calls tools in the app. On 2026-10-31 a printer connection failed because the app had found the printer in cloud mode, hid it from the model, and refused with "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now". That bug is fixed on this branch.

Kenneth, the product owner, then asked: do other tools have the same problem, where a refusal or an empty result fails to carry what the app saw? This report is the answer. Kenneth has not approved any fix.

A finding qualifies when both of these hold:
1. The app knew something more specific at that moment, or could have known it by reading its own state.
2. The model received a generic statement, a false statement, or an empty result that it cannot tell apart from a different situation.

A generic message does not qualify when the app itself received no reason.

## Where to look

- Branch `claude/printer-live-p1s`, commit `5f3bd2e59a`. It is `jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4` plus the connection fix (`ff2fee4fbd`, `ff10faa501`) and a test scenario. The `candidates`, `seen` and `search` code in findings 1 to 3 differs on `jusprin-newui`, which does not have the fix yet.
- This worktree also holds an uncommitted wording fix that changes sentence text only. It does not affect any finding.
- Paths below are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`.
- Make your own worktree from `5f3bd2e59a`. Do not build or edit in `.claude/worktrees/printer-live-p1s`, and never touch `.claude/worktrees/festive-lederberg-693438`.

## Rules for confirming

- Do not fix anything. Report only.
- No live-model runs: they cost money and Kenneth approves them batch by batch. None of these checks needs a model.
- Do not change Kenneth's real P1S (192.168.0.198). It stays in cloud mode with LAN Only off. Before any harness run against it, `lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` must print nothing, and `route -n get default` must show the Mac on the printer's 192.168.0.x network.
- Do not drive another running JusPrin. Use an isolated `--datadir`.
- Builds: check `uptime` and `pgrep -l ninja` first, use `-j4`, one build per directory, and never restart a build to change targets.
- Delete only your own harness data directory, by its printed path, never the `jusprin-shell-*` glob. Failed runs can leave API keys there.
- Temporary test edits and your notes stay uncommitted.
- A failure against a fake is weaker evidence than one against the real app or printer. Say which one you used.

## How to run the tools without a model

For findings 4 to 11, tools on MCP can be called directly. Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`, then use `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()`. It takes about 20 s per run. The full recipe and two traps are in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe.md`. One trap matters here: `slice_start` on an already sliced, unchanged plate has hung before.

The printer tools are not on MCP. For findings 1 to 3, use `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (the Bambu checks around line 5620) or `PrinterSetup` directly. `Testing/README.md` explains the Bambu fake.

---

## Serious: the model is told something false

### Finding 1: a failed Bambu LAN connection is reported with an unrelated reason

**What the app sees.** `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:2092-2105`. The plug-in reports `ConnectStatusFailed` with a code. The handler clears the selected printer (line 2096). For code `"5"` it erases the saved access code (lines 2099-2100) and shows the person "Incorrect password". For other codes it shows "Connect %s failed! [SN:%s, code=%s]". This handler is upstream OrcaSlicer: its commits `45bf4a99f1eb`, `e17c8bfb8009` and `d20656b8698e` are on `upstream/main`.

**What JusPrin does with it.** `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:493-524` never sees the failure or its code. It only sees what the handler left behind. These lines are fork code: `8334b3395ba` and `9f739dccf24` are on no upstream branch.

- **Code `"5"`, wrong access code.** Clearing the code makes `has_access_right()` false (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceManager.hpp:191`). `get_my_machine_list()` then omits the printer (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceCore/DevManager.cpp:663-673`), so `machine` at line 493 is null. The check at line 508 needs `machine != nullptr` and is skipped. Line 516 gives **"The printer is no longer available. Refresh the printer list and try again."**
- **Any other failure code, or `ConnectStatusLost`.** The code is kept, so `machine` is not null, but the selection is empty. Line 508 is true, and line 510 gives **"The selected printer changed. Select this printer again to reconnect."**

Either sentence reaches the model as "Connection to X failed: ..." (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:720-721`). The real reason never does. The access code being erased is also not reported.

**Existing test.** `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:5634-5637` checks the sentence, but it simulates a person changing the selection with `set_selected_machine("")`. It cannot tell that case from a failed connection.

**How to check.** `Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp` only ever sends `ConnectStatusOk` and `ConnectStatusLost` (lines 637, 655), so it needs a temporary change to send `connect_fn(ConnectStatusFailed, id, "5")`, and again with another code. Read `backend->connection(name)` afterwards. The real-printer version needs LAN Only on and a deliberately wrong code, so only Kenneth can do it.

**What would disprove it.** The attempt ends some other way first, or the machine stays in the list after a wrong code. I also have not confirmed that the real plug-in sends `"5"`; that comes from reading the handler.

### Finding 2: a Moonraker or OctoPrint test's real answer is thrown away

**What the app sees.** `src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp:77-82` fills `msg` from `format_error`, for example "HTTP 401: ...", a timeout, or an unresolvable host name (`src/slic3r/Utils/PrintHost.cpp:115`). Lines 92-97 also catch a host that answers but isn't Moonraker: "The host responded but it doesn't look like Moonraker". `src/slic3r/Utils/OctoPrint.cpp:160-163` does the same on error. Both are upstream code.

**What JusPrin does with it.** `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:625-626` declares `detail`, passes it to `host->test(detail)`, and keeps only true or false. Line 647 always says **"Could not reach the print host. Check its address, API key and network, then try again."** That is false when the host was reached and rejected the key, or when it is a different kind of service.

**How to check.** Run a small local HTTP server and call `connect_host(name, "moonraker", "127.0.0.1:<port>", "key")`, then read `connection(name).message` until it stops saying connecting. Try three cases: 401 on `/server/info`, 200 with `{}`, and the server stopped. I predict the same sentence all three times, while the log shows different errors.

**For whoever fixes it later.** `format_error` includes the response body, and some messages are translated, so the text would need bounding before the model reads it.

### Finding 3: the connection tools still hide printers they can see

**Where.** `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:481-492`. The loop drops these with no record:

| Dropped | Line | What the model is told |
|---|---|---|
| A printer of another model, such as a P1P when the person chose P1S | 482 | "found no printer of this model", which is literally true, but the likely explanation is hidden |
| A printer of the same model, when this saved printer is linked to a different one | 484 | "found no printer of this model", which is false |
| A printer of the same model already linked to another saved printer | 486-489 | "found no printer of this model", which is false |

The sentences are at `PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:479`, `481` and `776`. The tool's description says it "reports what it has found of that model so far" (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1600`), so the first row's limit is stated. The other two are not.

**How to check.** Use the fake with a second device of a different `printer_type`, then with a saved printer linked to another serial, then with two saved printers. Call `connection_status` and read `candidates`, `seen`, and the note posted after 15 s.

**A suspect I could not settle.** Line 489 also drops a printer in LAN mode whose `bind_state` isn't `"free"` (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceManager.hpp:233`). If a real LAN-mode printer can report `occupied`, that printer would be hidden too, and it is the one kind that can be connected. Whether that happens is unknown. It needs a printer in LAN mode, or a source saying what `DevBind` reports in that mode.

---

## Medium: the model can recover, but it is misled or wastes steps

### Finding 4: `export_file` says "Slice the plate first" while a slice is running

**Where.** `Workspace/OrcaOutputs.cpp:330-331`. Three different states give one answer, "Slice the plate first; it has no current G-code": never sliced, last slice refused or failed, and slicing right now.

**Why it matters.** The `needs_step` code tells the model to do the named step. During a slice, `slice_start` answers "A slice is already running. Wait for it, or ask again with preempt." (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2221`). My inference, not tested: a model following this could take over a slice the person started.

**How to check.** On MCP, call `slice_start`, then immediately `export_file` with kind `gcode`. Repeat on a plate whose slice was refused.

### Finding 5: `printer_list` omits a printer the network search can hear

**Where.** `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2272` reads `discover_printers(true)`, which is `get_my_machine_list()` (`PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp:113`). That list holds printers on the signed-in account, plus LAN-mode printers with an access code (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceCore/DevManager.cpp:651-675`). A cloud-mode printer that is announcing itself, with nobody signed in, isn't listed. This is Kenneth's P1S. The result is `items: []` with no reason, and the tool describes itself as listing "the physical printers this application knows about" (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1069`). It is available in the chats and on MCP.

**How to check.** With the printer heard (the log shows `UpdateLocalMachineInfo_WIFI`) and nobody signed in, call `printer_list`.

**Not settled.** Whether a saved Moonraker or OctoPrint printer appears. `src/slic3r/Utils/MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp:1322` announces one under some conditions, which I did not trace.

### Finding 6: the Add chat's "On the network now" line can be wrong in both directions

**Where.** `PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:215` reads `discover_printers()` once, when the panel opens, and `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts:188-189` writes "On the network now: ...".
- **Too many:** a printer on the person's account counts if it is online through the cloud, wherever it is (`PrinterDiscovery.cpp:113-116`). It may not be on this network.
- **Too few:** a printer announcing itself without an access code, and not on the account, isn't included. `discover_nearby_printers()` (`PrinterDiscovery.cpp:123`) exists for that and is used by the add form (`PrinterConversation.cpp:913`), not by this line.
- **Empty:** the line is left out, so the model has no statement either way.

**Correction to my first version.** I implied no search had run at that point. `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:998` and `1623` start discovery when the plug-in is set up, so one may already be running. I did not settle this.

**How to check.** Open an Add chat with a cloud-mode printer heard and nobody signed in, then read the first request in the request log (`<data dir>/jusprin/request-log`). Compare it with the add form's nearby list.

### Finding 7: `slice_inspect` answers `valid: false` with no reason (new since the first list)

**Where.** `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1685-1711` and `Workspace/OrcaOutputs.cpp:233`. Its sibling `slice_report` adds `sliceFailure` when the last slice failed (`Agent/ToolResults.cpp:795-800`). `slice_inspect` doesn't, so never sliced, refused, failed and slicing right now all look alike.

**A smaller case in the same tool.** `OrcaOutputs.cpp:238-256` opens the G-code file without checking that it opened. A missing file gives `valid: true` with empty text. That is rare.

**How to check.** On MCP, call `slice_inspect` on a plate whose slice was refused, and compare with `slice_report`.

### Finding 8: `slice_report` doesn't say a slice is running

**Where.** `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp` in `slice_report` (the comment reads "both answer no current slice"), and `Agent/ToolResults.cpp:795-800`. The description says only that an unsliced plate "says so".

**How much it matters.** When the model started the slice, `slice_start`'s note explains this. When the person started it, this tool gives no sign, though `workspace_inspect`'s slicing section does.

**Not settled.** Whether an old `sliceFailure` still shows during a new slice. I saw the failure erased at the end of a run (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:935`, `950`) but did not trace the start.

**How to check.** Start a slice outside the tool, call `slice_report` while it runs, and repeat after a refused slice.

---

## Low

### Finding 9: `print_dialog_open` drops a slice failure it just looked up

**Where.** `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2105-2107`. `targets_sliced` fills `failure`, and then the message says only "This plate has no valid slice. Slice it with slice_start first".

**Why it is low (I rated this medium at first).** The model has usually been told already: the `slice-failed` skill fires on a failed slice, `workspace_inspect` includes `sliceFailure` per plate (`Agent/ToolResults.cpp:722`), and calling `slice_start` again returns the reason. The cost is a wasted step.

### Finding 10: `presets_list` doesn't count hidden presets

**Where.** `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2328`. Hidden presets are skipped, so an installed but hidden filament gives `total: 0`, the same as one that doesn't exist. The compatibility filter is stated in the tool's description, and the model can ask for all. The hidden filter can't be turned off. The description says "this installation offers", so this may be intended. Commit `09cc63eaa9` accepts a hidden preset by name when the project uses it.

### Finding 11: `settings_search` is silent when a setting is in another scope

**Where.** `Workspace/SettingsSupport.hpp:127-146` with `Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp:89`. Searching printer settings for a process setting gives `items: []` and no hint. By contrast, `settings_get` on a wrong key gives suggestions (`Workspace/OrcaSettings.hpp:24`).

---

## Withdrawn or outside the list

- **Plug-in install, withdrawn.** My first list said the model is told nothing when the installer is closed or the download fails (`PrinterConversation.cpp:253-256`). That is true, but no model turn is running at that moment, the person has seen the installer's own dialog, and the next request's instructions correctly say "Bambu's network plug-in: not installed" (`printerInstructions.ts:210-212`). Nothing false reaches the model.
- **`print_dialog_open` success, a related case.** It reports `opened: true` and "The app's send dialog is open" before the dialog opens, which happens later in a `CallAfter` (`Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2116-2124`, `Shell/ShellController.cpp`). If the plate has gone by then, the person sees a message and the model still believes the dialog opened. This is a false success rather than a refusal, and it should be rare.
- **"Choose a matching printer from the refreshed list."** `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:547` can occur if a printer vanishes while the person types the code. The app knows little more than that. Not counted.

## Reviewed and not counted

- **The reason is passed on:** `project_open` and the import tools (the app's messages travel in `report`), `slice_start` (`reason`), failed settings changes (issues with codes), `object_repair`, G-code export (the copy error), and the print-again refusals in `Shell/ShellController.cpp`. The Bambu search states are reported since `ff2fee4fbd`.
- **The app has no more to give:** 3MF export returning below 0, STL write returning false, "The app rendered nothing", and "The app did not generate the test". A calibration the person cancelled looks like that same failure, and the generator returns nothing to tell them apart.
- **Refusals that just need a fresh read:** `not_found` and `stale_workspace` say what to read again.
- **Settings hidden from reading:** I had this as unconfirmed. The seven connection keys in `kWithheldSettings` (`Workspace/SettingsSupport.hpp`) are not filtered from `settings_search` by this code path, and `settings_get` refuses them with a stated reason, so nothing is silently hidden.

## Limits of this sweep

- I read every refusal message in `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`, `Workspace/*.cpp` and `PrinterSetup/`, but not every successful result.
- `object_analyze`: I read its failure handling, not each section. Empty sections there appear to be measurements, not states, but I did not check them one by one.
- `workspace_inspect`: I read the printer section, not all of it.
- I did not sweep the filament chat beyond its refusals in `PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp`, or `view_render` beyond its failure messages.
- Severity is my judgement. Rare-failure cases should be weighed against Kenneth's standing preference for a generic error on rare or speculative failures.

## Corrections since the list sent to Kenneth in chat

| In the chat list | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|
| #1 said a wrong access code gives "The selected printer changed" | Finding 1: a wrong code gives "The printer is no longer available"; other failures give "selected printer changed" | Erasing the code removes the printer from the list, which changes the branch taken |
| #1 "didn't check upstream or fork" | Settled: the handler is upstream, the sentences are fork | `git branch -r --contains` |
| #4 `print_dialog_open`, medium | Finding 9, low | The model has usually already been told |
| #8 implied no search had run | Finding 6, unsettled | Discovery may start with the plug-in |
| #9 plug-in install | Withdrawn | The next request states it correctly |
| Not listed | Finding 7, `slice_inspect` | Found while covering the gaps |
| Not listed | The suspect in finding 3 | I dismissed it too early: the `free` override applies only to `farm` |
| "not confirmed" on settings hidden from search | Settled, not a finding | Code path read |

The chat list's numbers map to this report as follows: 1→1, 2→2, 3→3, 4→9, 5→4, 6→8, 7→5, 8→6, 9→withdrawn, 10→10, 11→11.

## What to report back

For each finding, give one of: **confirmed**, **partly right** (say what is wrong), **wrong**, or **could not test** (say why). Include the code you read or the output you saw, whether you used a fake or the real thing, and the exact message the model received. List anything this sweep missed. Keep it in plain English and do not propose fixes unless asked.

---
name: manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe
description: "Reproduce any JusPrin tool behaviour without a live model in about 20 s per run: shell harness --manual-mcp plus tests/mcp/probe.py call(); two traps (leaked harness from `cd && cmd &`, slice_start on an unchanged sliced plate)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 0b03c379-ea3d-491e-a0b3-9b5bf2a6240f
  modified: 2026-10-12T23:51:00.507Z
---

Used 2026-10-12 for the spiral vase investigation (branch `claude/spiral-vase-writable`).

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. The fixture is two plates, one 20 mm box each, Bambu X1C 0.4, "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C", "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", the same presets as Kenneth's live tests. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

**Slice waits, 2026-10-15 (jusprin-newui 336facf825).** Trap 2 re-measured: `slice_start {plateId, wait: true}` on the sliced, unchanged plate 1 got no reply in 120 s (a hang, follow-up task filed). Right after `printer_setup` fixes a plate Orca had refused, `slice_start` fails "That plate cannot be sliced as it stands" for about 3 s: the adapter checks `PartPlate::can_slice()`, whose invalid flag Orca refreshes only on its next deferred validation. A refused slice hanging the wait was fixed on branch `claude/slice-wait-refused` (worktree brave-panini-347b62): `WorkspaceSlicing::refused` carries Orca's ValidateError text. Over MCP every `unavailable_operation` reads as `workspace_unavailable` (McpProtocol.cpp), so don't take that code to mean JusPrin is closed.

description: "Reproduce any JusPrin tool behaviour without a live model in about 20 s per run: shell harness --manual-mcp plus tests/mcp/probe.py call(); two traps (leaked harness from `cd && cmd &`, slice_start on an unchanged sliced plate)"

Used 2026-10-12 for the spiral vase investigation (branch `claude/spiral-vase-writable`).

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. The fixture is two plates, one 20 mm box each, Bambu X1C 0.4, "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C", "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", the same presets as Kenneth's live tests. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

**Slice waits, 2026-10-15 (jusprin-newui 336facf825).** Trap 2 re-measured: `slice_start {plateId, wait: true}` on the sliced, unchanged plate 1 got no reply in 120 s (a hang, follow-up task filed). Right after `printer_setup` fixes a plate Orca had refused, `slice_start` fails "That plate cannot be sliced as it stands" for about 3 s: the adapter checks `PartPlate::can_slice()`, whose invalid flag Orca refreshes only on its next deferred validation. A refused slice hanging the wait was fixed on branch `claude/slice-wait-refused` (worktree brave-panini-347b62): `WorkspaceSlicing::refused` carries Orca's ValidateError text. Over MCP every `unavailable_operation` reads as `workspace_unavailable` (McpProtocol.cpp), so don't take that code to mean JusPrin is closed.

# One live chat against the real P1S, 2026-11-01

Code under test: `claude/festive-lederberg-693438` (`ff2fee4fbd`, `ff10faa501`) plus the
scenario on `claude/printer-live-p1s`. Provider anthropic, model `claude-sonnet-5-5` as read
from the run's app config; the app's log does not record the model name in a request or
response, so that config line is the evidence. Printer: Bambu Lab P1S at 192.168.0.198,
cloud mode, not changed. Ran once, 09:01:48 to 09:02:46 PST.

## Verdict

The model told the truth about the printer and what to do. After the app's note it said the
P1S was found at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off, that it cannot connect as it is, that
LAN Only is turned on in the printer's network settings, and that connecting is optional.
It never said there is no printer on the network and gave no menu path.

Things to know:

- At +25 s, 6 seconds before the printer was heard, it said "The app didn't find your P1S on
  the network" after the app's 15-second note. True of what had been observed, but it does
  not say the search is still running, and it asked the person to go and look at the printer.
- It repeated the app's sentence that "the printer can prepare prints without a connection".
  The printer does not prepare prints; the app does. The wording comes from `kPersonsChoice` in
  PrinterConversation.cpp, so the model is faithful to a misleading line. "Network settings" also
  comes from the app's tool description; nobody checked it on the printer in this run.
- It never called `printer_connect`, so no model read the new refusal text in this run.
- The model did not ask for the address; the scenario volunteered it at +37 s.

## Checks

Five of six word and outcome checks passed. `live_p1s_words_invent_no_menu_path` failed on a false
positive: my word list had " menu" and the model said "Connect… in its menu on Home", a real app
menu named in printerInstructions.ts. The list was then narrowed; that narrowing has only been
compiled and checked against this saved transcript, since no second live chat is allowed.

## The first no-model check missed the printer

Before the chat I ran the free `--printer-network-check` twice with this new binary. The first run,
about 08:57, heard nothing for 120 seconds while reporting search state `listening` and failed. A
plain Python listener at 09:00 heard three announcements in 45 seconds. The second run, just after,
heard the printer at 25 s and passed. Cause unknown. My hypothesis, unverified: macOS Local Network
permission on a new executable's first run.

## Output of the run, word for word

The first model line at +0s is the page's opening, not a model request. "model: " with nothing after
it is a model turn that only called a tool.

===== jusprin-worktree-build
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).
===== tool-error-contract
---
name: tool-error-contract
description: "2026-10-21 Kenneth's decisions on tool error codes; one list in Agent/ToolErrors.hpp, same codes in-app and MCP, no changed/next fields; committed 29ae944fea, merged to local jusprin-newui (unpushed)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 76cfae73-9bbb-4d38-9b41-2b6a0df916c5
  modified: 2026-10-21T21:05:26.062Z
---

Kenneth chose the full contract (option a) for tool errors on 2026-10-21. Implemented as one commit, 29ae944fea, on branch `claude/tool-error-contract` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-error-contract`, cut from bed54fd8fe). Fast-forwarded onto `jusprin-newui` the same day and pushed. The branch and worktree were deleted after the merge; the follow-up 9ad6bb927f (workspace_inspect shows disabled copies) sits on top.

His answers to the five open decisions:
- D2: no `changed` or `next` fields in the error envelope. Messages carry the outcome.
- D3: one spelling of each code on both surfaces; MCP no longer renames codes.
- D4: a busy OrcaSlicer keeps failing (`busy`); the tool does not wait.
- D5: `local_save_failed` stays a failure even when the change ran.
- D6: report partial changes in the message (no rollback); prefer checking before changing.

**Why:** a code that means one next step, truthful about what changed, is what a model can act on; the old `unavailable_operation` → `workspace_unavailable` rename told MCP clients JusPrin was closed.

**How to apply:** a new failure picks a code from `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp` (`fail()` throws on any other), and an "impossible" state throws instead of failing. Don't propose `changed`/`next` fields again. Background and inventory: the untracked `tool-error-reporting-sweep.md` in the main checkout. Related: [[rare-failures-get-a-generic-error]], [[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]].
===== rare-failures-get-a-generic-error
---
name: rare-failures-get-a-generic-error
description: "Kenneth 2026-10-15 — rare, speculative failure paths (save failures etc.) get one generic error; don't design per-cause handling, retries or prompt rules for them"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ef1c9e7b-9046-4021-b7fe-b659d08d3643
  modified: 2026-10-15T20:51:18.020Z
---

On 2026-10-15 Kenneth reviewed my nozzle-change proposal. It had per-cause error messages, prompt rules and handling for save failures caused by a full disk, an open paint tool or a not-yet-drawn canvas. He said those cases were wrong, speculative or rare, and that they should simply get a generic error.

**Why:** they are hard to handle well and almost never happen. The effort belongs on failures people actually hit, like the printer panel's action-id collision, which I reproduced.

**How to apply:** before proposing handling for a failure, ask whether a real person will plausibly hit it. If it's rare or unreproduced, recommend the existing generic error and move on. Don't list speculative causes as if they were findings. Related: [[report-outcomes-not-obstacles]], [[printer-panel-action-id-collision]].
===== fake-bambu-printer-sim

description: "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.{hpp,cpp} — the in-process Bambu printer stand-in that IS on jusprin-newui (unlike the Moonraker simulator); keeps a real Bambu system preset selected and substitutes only the agent."

---

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. Wait for `!is_adding_script_handler()`, a non-busy page and a URL, as the old `setup_manual` check did.
- **Open the panel through `ShellController::open_printer_conversation`** in live tests; `PrinterPanel::open` skips the full-window layout.
- **The model's reliability is measured, not assumed.** gpt-5.4-mini saved changes without waiting for yes in 6 of 10 runs, even with an explicit "ask, then stop" prompt. Count across several runs before calling prompt wording fixed.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]].

**2026-10-21, opens ignored since 2026-09-29:** `ShellController::open_printer_conversation` returns without opening while a task chat is open (guard from bb29582ff7), and `PrinterPanel::close` finishes in a CallAfter that clears that flag. ===== check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
---
name: check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
description: "2026-10-21 one idle session left four overlapping nohup Release builds in one build dir, pegging all 12 cores for an hour; pgrep ninja on the build dir before launching, and kill your builds before ending a turn"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: a697178b-3815-42ff-b8cb-a240eb240688
  modified: 2026-10-21T19:02:35.660Z
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.

metadata:

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. **Queue order trap (2026-10-21):** PrinterPanel::close finishes via the panel's own CallAfter; an open queued with wxGetApp().CallAfter can run first (separate queues, no order) and is refused. Queue with live_panel()->CallAfter.

---
name: check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
description: "2026-10-21 one idle session left four overlapping nohup Release builds in one build dir, pegging all 12 cores for an hour; pgrep ninja on the build dir before launching, and kill your builds before ending a turn"
metadata:

  originSessionId: a697178b-3815-42ff-b8cb-a240eb240688
  modified: 2026-10-21T19:02:35.660Z
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.

#pragma once

// Every code a tool call can fail with. The in-app agent and MCP clients read
// the same spelling. Each code stands for one next step, named in the comment
// above its group; the message says what happened, including what a call that
// stopped part-way had already changed. ToolExecutionCoordinator::fail refuses
// a code that is not listed here, so a new failure picks the code whose next
// step fits instead of inventing one. The table in the tool guide's "Error
// codes" section lists the same codes for people.

#include <algorithm>
#include <iterator>
#include <string_view>

namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Agent::ToolErrors {

inline constexpr std::string_view kCodes[] = {
    // Fix the arguments and call again.
    "invalid_arguments",
    "unknown_tool",
    "unknown_skill",
    // Not run because an earlier call of the same response failed; decide again.
    "not_run",
    // Read the state again, then call again.
    "not_found",       // an id that is not in the open project
    "stale_workspace", // the project changed since the read the call was based on
    "feature_expired", // a face, edge or hole handle from an earlier revision
    "connection_lost", // MCP bridge only: the outcome is unknown
    // Wait, then call again.
    "busy",
    // Do the step the message names first, with another tool.
    "needs_step",
    // Ask the person: the decision or the action is theirs.
    "opened_before",
    "workspace_unavailable", // no open project, or no FFF printer selected
    // Stop and tell the person.
    "refused",           // OrcaSlicer does not do this here
    "failed",            // OrcaSlicer tried and failed
    "local_save_failed", // the project could not be saved
    "cancelled",

    // The settings tools' corrections (tool guide, "Error codes").
    "unknown_setting",
    "unsupported_scope",
    "invalid_setting_value",
    "incompatible_settings",
    "unsupported_setting_mutation",
    "withheld_setting",
    "unknown_preset",
    "incompatible_preset",
    "unsupported_plate",
    "not_selected",
    "read_only_preset",
    "name_taken",
    "invalid_preset_name",
    "not_in_project",

    // The printer and filament chats' own refusals.
    "unknown_nozzle",
    "not_in_this_conversation",
    "no_printer",
    "other_printer",
    "stock_profile",
    "unknown_printer",
    "connection_unavailable",
    "unknown_device",
    "address_needed",
    "too_many",
    "already_added",
    "add_failed",
    "change_failed",
    "nothing_to_change",
    "not_saved",

    // The internal record tools, which only the page calls.
    "slice_required",
    "missing_plate",
    "missing_build",
    "invalid_progress",
};

inline bool registered(std::string_view code)
{
    return std::find(std::begin(kCodes), std::end(kCodes), code) != std::end(kCodes);
}

} // namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Agent::ToolErrors

# One live chat against the real P1S, 2026-11-01

Code under test: `claude/festive-lederberg-693438` (`ff2fee4fbd`, `ff10faa501`) plus the
scenario on `claude/printer-live-p1s`. Provider anthropic, model `claude-sonnet-5-5` as read
from the run's app config; the app's log does not record the model name in a request or
response, so that config line is the evidence. Printer: Bambu Lab P1S at 192.168.0.198,
cloud mode, not changed. Ran once, 09:01:48 to 09:02:46 PST.

## Verdict

The model told the truth about the printer and what to do. After the app's note it said the
P1S was found at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off, that it cannot connect as it is, that
LAN Only is turned on in the printer's network settings, and that connecting is optional.
It never said there is no printer on the network and gave no menu path.

Things to know:

- At +25 s, 6 seconds before the printer was heard, it said "The app didn't find your P1S on
  the network" after the app's 15-second note. True of what had been observed, but it does
  not say the search is still running, and it asked the person to go and look at the printer.
- It repeated the app's sentence that "the printer can prepare prints without a connection".
  The printer does not prepare prints; the app does. The wording comes from `kPersonsChoice` in
  PrinterConversation.cpp, so the model is faithful to a misleading line. "Network settings" also
  comes from the app's tool description; nobody checked it on the printer in this run.
- It never called `printer_connect`, so no model read the new refusal text in this run.
- The model did not ask for the address; the scenario volunteered it at +37 s.

## Checks

Five of six word and outcome checks passed. `live_p1s_words_invent_no_menu_path` failed on a false
positive: my word list had " menu" and the model said "Connect… in its menu on Home", a real app
menu named in printerInstructions.ts. The list was then narrowed; that narrowing has only been
compiled and checked against this saved transcript, since no second live chat is allowed.

## The first no-model check missed the printer

Before the chat I ran the free `--printer-network-check` twice with this new binary. The first run,
about 08:57, heard nothing for 120 seconds while reporting search state `listening` and failed. A
plain Python listener at 09:00 heard three announcements in 45 seconds. The second run, just after,
heard the printer at 25 s and passed. Cause unknown. My hypothesis, unverified: macOS Local Network
permission on a new executable's first run.

## Output of the run, word for word

The first model line at +0s is the page's opening, not a model request. "model: " with nothing after
it is a model turn that only called a tool.

## What changed and what did not

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. On 2026-09-23 this was first blamed on the product and "fixed" with a deferral, then traced to the test and reverted. Wait for `!is_adding_script_handler()`, a non-busy page and a URL, as the old `setup_manual` check did.
- **Open the panel through `ShellController::open_printer_conversation`** in live tests; `PrinterPanel::open` skips the full-window layout.
- **The model's reliability is measured, not assumed.** gpt-5.4-mini saved changes without waiting for yes in 6 of 10 runs, even with an explicit "ask, then stop" prompt. Count across several runs before calling prompt wording fixed.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]].

**2026-10-21, opens ignored since 2026-09-29:** `ShellController::open_printer_conversation` returns without opening while a task chat is open (guard from bb29582ff7), and `PrinterPanel::close` finishes in a CallAfter that clears that flag.
