5:JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.
79:**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.
99:**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.
105:**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.
109:**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.
121:1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.
133:An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

- For `2025-03-26`, it also leaves out `structuredContent`, and leaves `outputSchema` and `title` out of the catalog. The serialized text result is kept.
- For the later supported revisions, `structuredContent` and `title` are kept.

No negotiated version advertises `outputSchema` any more (see [tool budget and tool shape](#tool-budget-and-tool-shape)). The bridge still has its own code that strips the field, because the bridge also forwards catalogs from a live app of another version. These adjustments are deliberate, for compatibility. They are not conflicting definitions of the same tool.

### Image results

Three read tools in the candidate catalog return a picture: `project_attachment_read` (a reference image), `view_render` (the prepared or sliced scene), and `printer_camera_snapshot`. The result that the registry produces holds the encoded image and a structured block that describes it (dimensions, camera or layer range, capture time). Each adapter then presents that one result in its own format:

- MCP: an `image` content block next to the text and the structured result. `2025-03-26` gets the same block, because image content is older than structured content.
- OpenAI: the text and the structured block are the function result. The image is appended as an image input in the continuation, because a function result can only be text.

The two adapters present the same result in different formats. The tool itself does not behave differently. Both projections must be tested before the first tool that returns an image ships. Limit every image to 1280 pixels on the long edge and to 2 MB, so that one frame never takes up most of the context window. Never return an image the user has not allowed. A camera frame requires the privacy grant in Printer Configuration. Without it, the call fails with `camera_disabled`.

## Errors should teach the next valid call

When an invalid state is expected, handle it with ordinary control flow and return a structured error. Do not throw an exception. An error should say what the problem is and include only the data the Agent needs to correct the call.

An error is judged by four things, in this order:

1. **It says truthfully what happened, including whether anything changed.** A failed call changed nothing, unless its message says what it had already changed when it stopped. A tool that can stop part-way says so in its message (`printer_setup` names the printer it already selected and the edits it dropped; `object_repair` names the paint it removed and the parts it repaired). Prefer checking everything before changing anything, so that a refusal never comes part-way: `plate_layout` checks the plate limit, copies of a disabled object, and an open editing tool before it applies any row.
2. **It names the next step and who takes it,** through its code (below) and its message.
3. **The same situation gets the same code from every tool.** A plate id that is not in the open project is `not_found` from `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`, `export_file`, `plate_layout`, `project_delete_items` and the import tools.
4. **A broken invariant is not reported to the model.** A state the code guarantees cannot happen (a tool with no handler, a coordinator without the product state every app host gives it, a checked id that does not parse) throws, so it reaches Sentry.

Every code a tool can fail with is listed in `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`, and `ToolExecutionCoordinator::fail` throws on any other. The in-app agent and MCP clients read the same codes: the MCP adapter passes them through unchanged. Each code stands for one next step:

- For `2025-03-26`, it also leaves out `structuredContent`, and leaves `outputSchema` and `title` out of the catalog. The serialized text result is kept.
- For the later supported revisions, `structuredContent` and `title` are kept.

No negotiated version advertises `outputSchema` any more (see [tool budget and tool shape](#tool-budget-and-tool-shape)). The bridge still has its own code that strips the field, because the bridge also forwards catalogs from a live app of another version. These adjustments are deliberate, for compatibility. They are not conflicting definitions of the same tool.

### Image results

Three read tools in the candidate catalog return a picture: `project_attachment_read` (a reference image), `view_render` (the prepared or sliced scene), and `printer_camera_snapshot`. The result that the registry produces holds the encoded image and a structured block that describes it (dimensions, camera or layer range, capture time). Each adapter then presents that one result in its own format:

- MCP: an `image` content block next to the text and the structured result. `2025-03-26` gets the same block, because image content is older than structured content.
- OpenAI: the text and the structured block are the function result. The image is appended as an image input in the continuation, because a function result can only be text.

The two adapters present the same result in different formats. The tool itself does not behave differently. Both projections must be tested before the first tool that returns an image ships. Limit every image to 1280 pixels on the long edge and to 2 MB, so that one frame never takes up most of the context window. Never return an image the user has not allowed. A camera frame requires the privacy grant in Printer Configuration. Without it, the call fails with `camera_disabled`.

## Errors should teach the next valid call

When an invalid state is expected, handle it with ordinary control flow and return a structured error. Do not throw an exception. An error should say what the problem is and include only the data the Agent needs to correct the call.

An error is judged by four things, in this order:

1. **It says truthfully what happened, including whether anything changed.** A failed call changed nothing, unless its message says what it had already changed when it stopped. A tool that can stop part-way says so in its message (`printer_setup` names the printer it already selected and the edits it dropped; `object_repair` names the paint it removed and the parts it repaired). Prefer checking everything before changing anything, so that a refusal never comes part-way: `plate_layout` checks the plate limit, copies of a disabled object, and an open editing tool before it applies any row.
2. **It names the next step and who takes it,** through its code (below) and its message.
3. **The same situation gets the same code from every tool.** A plate id that is not in the open project is `not_found` from `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`, `export_file`, `plate_layout`, `project_delete_items` and the import tools.
4. **A broken invariant is not reported to the model.** A state the code guarantees cannot happen (a tool with no handler, a coordinator without the product state every app host gives it, a checked id that does not parse) throws, so it reaches Sentry.

Every code a tool can fail with is listed in `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`, and `ToolExecutionCoordinator::fail` throws on any other. The in-app agent and MCP clients read the same codes: the MCP adapter passes them through unchanged. Each code stands for one next step:

content.content:
**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.
**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

content.content:
An error is judged by four things, in this order:

1. **It says truthfully what happened, including whether anything changed.** A failed call changed nothing, unless its message says what it had already changed when it stopped. A tool that can stop part-way says so in its message (`printer_setup` names the printer it already selected and the edits it dropped; `object_repair` names the paint it removed and the parts it repaired). Prefer checking everything before changing anything, so that a refusal never comes part-way: `plate_layout` checks the plate limit, copies of a disabled object, and an open editing tool before it applies any row.
2. **It names the next step and who takes it,** through its code (below) and its message.
3. **The same situation gets the same code from every tool.** A plate id that is not in the open project is `not_found` from `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`, `export_file`, `plate_layout`, `project_delete_items` and the import tools.

An error is judged by four things, in this order:

1. **It says truthfully what happened, including whether anything changed.** A failed call changed nothing, unless its message says what it had already changed when it stopped. A tool that can stop part-way says so in its message (`printer_setup` names the printer it already selected and the edits it dropped; `object_repair` names the paint it removed and the parts it repaired). Prefer checking everything before changing anything, so that a refusal never comes part-way: `plate_layout` checks the plate limit, copies of a disabled object, and an open editing tool before it applies any row.
2. **It names the next step and who takes it,** through its code (below) and its message.
3. **The same situation gets the same code from every tool.** A plate id that is not in the open project is `not_found` from `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`, `export_file`, `plate_layout`, `project_delete_items` and the import tools.

Two new causes came up and are named where they apply: (5) an I/O result is not checked; (6) the result is written before the work happens.

Shared plumbing that every table relies on:

- `workspace_error_code()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:62-83) maps `WorkspaceError` kinds one to one onto codes: NotFound and InvalidId to `not_found`, StaleId and StaleSettings to `stale_workspace`, Busy to `busy`, NeedsStep to `needs_step`, Refused to `refused`, Failed to `failed`, WorkspaceUnavailable to `workspace_unavailable`, InvalidArgument to `invalid_arguments`, FeatureExpired to `feature_expired`. The message is the adapter's own text, so the collapses below are the adapter's, not the mapping's.
- `targets_sliced()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1054-1069) says whether every plate named (all plates when none is named) has `sliced == true`, and copies the first `slice_failure` it meets into `failure`. It starts from `sliced = !snapshot.plates.empty()`, so a plateId that matches no plate leaves `sliced` true.
- `WorkspacePlate::sliced` is `PartPlate::is_slice_result_valid()` read on every snapshot (Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1093); `slicing.running` is `Plater::is_background_process_slicing()`, which is the app-wide `p->m_is_slicing` flag (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:18402-18405). There is one slicing process for the whole app.
- `slice_failure` on a plate is the fork's own record (`m_slice_failures`), written by `record_slice_failure()` (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:977-1004) when OrcaSlicer calls the fork's `report_slice_declined()` hook or when a run ends with `event.error()`. The text comes from the print-issue monitor's first Blocker (`PrintIssues/PrintIssue.cpp:90-111`) or falls back to `"The app did not start slicing this plate."` (refused) or `"The slice stopped with an error."` (failed). The record is erased when the plate becomes sliced (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:935) and when a run starts on the current plate (948-950), and hidden from the snapshot while that plate is slicing (1115-1116).
- `report_slice_declined()` is called from three of OrcaSlicer's exits in `Plater::reslice()` and `Plater::start_next_slice()` (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:16070, 16116, 16262). Two other early returns in `reslice()` call nothing: the gizmo-in-editing-mode return (16076-16078) and the "could not stop UI job within 10000 ms" return (16082-16087). The "background process in idle state, use previous result" branch (16153-16165) also calls nothing; it sets the plate valid when it has printable instances and invalid when it has none.

# Tool result inventory: slice, export, print and inspect tools

Read from the worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-silent-failures` at commit 5f3bd2e59a, code only; nothing was built or run. Paths are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Line numbers are from this commit.

Vocabulary: a "collapse" is two or more states the app can tell apart at the moment it answers, which the model receives as the same result. Causes are numbered as in the earlier analysis: (1) fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event; (2) a filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason; (3) tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined; (4) a generic error was used for a common, distinguishable state. Two new causes came up and are named where they apply: (5) an I/O result is not checked; (6) the result is written before the work happens.

Shared plumbing that every table relies on:

- `workspace_error_code()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:62-83) maps `WorkspaceError` kinds one to one onto codes: NotFound and InvalidId to `not_found`, StaleId and StaleSettings to `stale_workspace`, Busy to `busy`, NeedsStep to `needs_step`, Refused to `refused`, Failed to `failed`, WorkspaceUnavailable to `workspace_unavailable`, InvalidArgument to `invalid_arguments`, FeatureExpired to `feature_expired`. The message is the adapter's own text, so the collapses below are the adapter's, not the mapping's.
- `targets_sliced()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1054-1069) says whether every plate named (all plates when none is named) has `sliced == true`, and copies the first `slice_failure` it meets into `failure`. It starts from `sliced = !snapshot.plates.empty()`, so a plateId that matches no plate leaves `sliced` true.
- `WorkspacePlate::sliced` is `PartPlate::is_slice_result_valid()` read on every snapshot (Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1093); `slicing.running` is `Plater::is_background_process_slicing()`, which is the app-wide `p->m_is_slicing` flag (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:18402-18405). There is one slicing process for the whole app.
- `slice_failure` on a plate is the fork's own record (`m_slice_failures`), written by `record_slice_failure()` (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:977-1004) when OrcaSlicer calls the fork's `report_slice_declined()` hook or when a run ends with `event.error()`. The text comes from the print-issue monitor's first Blocker (`PrintIssues/PrintIssue.cpp:90-111`) or falls back to `"The app did not start slicing this plate."` (refused) or `"The slice stopped with an error."` (failed). The record is erased when the plate becomes sliced (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:935) and when a run starts on the current plate (948-950), and hidden from the snapshot while that plate is slicing (1115-1116).
- `report_slice_declined()` is called from three of OrcaSlicer's exits in `Plater::reslice()` and `Plater::start_next_slice()` (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:16070, 16116, 16262). Two other early returns in `reslice()` call nothing: the gizmo-in-editing-mode return (16076-16078) and the "could not stop UI job within 10000 ms" return (16082-16087). The "background process in idle state, use previous result" branch (16153-16165) also calls nothing; it sets the plate valid when it has printable instances and invalid when it has none.

# Tool result inventory: slice, export, print and inspect tools

Read from the worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-silent-failures` at commit 5f3bd2e59a, code only; nothing was built or run. Paths are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Line numbers are from this commit.

Vocabulary: a "collapse" is two or more states the app can tell apart at the moment it answers, which the model receives as the same result. Causes are numbered as in the earlier analysis: (1) fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event; (2) a filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason; (3) tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined; (4) a generic error was used for a common, distinguishable state. Two new causes came up and are named where they apply: (5) an I/O result is not checked; (6) the result is written before the work happens.

Shared plumbing that every table relies on:

- `workspace_error_code()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:62-83) maps `WorkspaceError` kinds one to one onto codes: NotFound and InvalidId to `not_found`, StaleId and StaleSettings to `stale_workspace`, Busy to `busy`, NeedsStep to `needs_step`, Refused to `refused`, Failed to `failed`, WorkspaceUnavailable to `workspace_unavailable`, InvalidArgument to `invalid_arguments`, FeatureExpired to `feature_expired`. The message is the adapter's own text, so the collapses below are the adapter's, not the mapping's.
- `targets_sliced()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1054-1069) says whether every plate named (all plates when none is named) has `sliced == true`, and copies the first `slice_failure` it meets into `failure`. It starts from `sliced = !snapshot.plates.empty()`, so a plateId that matches no plate leaves `sliced` true.
- `WorkspacePlate::sliced` is `PartPlate::is_slice_result_valid()` read on every snapshot (Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1093); `slicing.running` is `Plater::is_background_process_slicing()`, which is the app-wide `p->m_is_slicing` flag (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:18402-18405). There is one slicing process for the whole app.
- `slice_failure` on a plate is the fork's own record (`m_slice_failures`), written by `record_slice_failure()` (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:977-1004) when OrcaSlicer calls the fork's `report_slice_declined()` hook or when a run ends with `event.error()`. The text comes from the print-issue monitor's first Blocker (`PrintIssues/PrintIssue.cpp:90-111`) or falls back to `"The app did not start slicing this plate."` (refused) or `"The slice stopped with an error."` (failed). The record is erased when the plate becomes sliced (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:935) and when a run starts on the current plate (948-950), and hidden from the snapshot while that plate is slicing (1115-1116).
- `report_slice_declined()` is called from three of OrcaSlicer's exits in `Plater::reslice()` and `Plater::start_next_slice()` (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:16070, 16116, 16262). Two other early returns in `reslice()` call nothing: the gizmo-in-editing-mode return (16076-16078) and the "could not stop UI job within 10000 ms" return (16082-16087). The "background process in idle state, use previous result" branch (16153-16165) also calls nothing; it sets the plate valid when it has printable instances and invalid when it has none.

## Collapses by cause

Cause (1), fork reads leftover state instead of the event:
- `slice_start`'s `started` and `alreadySliced` are read from `slicing.running` and `is_slice_result_valid()` after the posted event returns. Two of OrcaSlicer's silent exits in `reslice()` (gizmo editing, UI job not stopped) and the idle branch have no `report_slice_declined()` hook, so they produce the generic refusal or a wrong `alreadySliced`. The live anomaly (sliced plate answered "refused", then `sliced: false`) sits here; its writer is unverified.
- `export_file`, `slice_inspect`, `slice_report` read the app-wide `is_background_process_slicing()` and refuse a valid plate while another plate slices.
- A cancelled run records nothing (`on_process_completed` keys on `event.error()`), so cancel, never sliced and "invalidated, cause unknown" collapse in the slicing section and in `activity_cancel`.
- A run start erases the plate's recorded failure (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:948-950); a cancelled retry therefore loses the reason the model had.

Cause (2), a filter drops the reason:
- `print_dialog_open` fills `failure` and drops it (confirmed (9)).
- `slice_report` with `valid: false` and no record does not say which of never / stale / running it is, although the snapshot has `estimateStatus`.
- `activity_cancel` uses one sentence for four endings of the tools' run, and `not_found` for a handle the tools issued and then superseded.
- `slicing.plates[].sliceFailure` is the short form (no `code`, `objectName`, `sequence`); only `slice_report` has the full one.
- `sliceWarnings` absent means both "none" and "never read while active" for a non-active plate.
- `slice_report` leaves a section out when the check could not run, same as when it was not asked.

Cause (3), fakes only produce imagined states: see the test section.

Cause (4), a generic error for a common, distinguishable state:
- `export_file`'s one `needs_step` sentence for never / stale / refused / failed / running (confirmed (4)).
- `slice_inspect`'s bare `{"valid": false}` for the same five (confirmed (7)).
- `slice_start`'s synthesized "The app did not start slicing this plate." whenever no Blocker is in the monitor.
- `export_file` presets: "the preset files exist" for any empty result (probable, unverified).

New cause (5), an I/O result is not checked: `slice_inspect` view gcode opens the file without `is_open()` and answers `valid: true, gcode: ""` (confirmed (7)).

New cause (6), the result is written before the work happens: `print_dialog_open` answers `opened: true` before its `CallAfter`; the deferred open can fail silently (`!m_installed`), show the person an error dialog (plate gone, including a plateId that was never in the project), or decline (`print_again` state moved), and no channel carries that back.

Stated in a description (plausibly intended): `busy` for a running slice and that nobody knows whose run it is; `export_file` needing a sliced plate; `slice_report` and `slice_inspect` saying "not sliced"; `slice_report` returning `valid: false` during a run (stated in `slice_start`'s text only); `print_dialog_open`'s `needs_step` and "opens after the call returns"; `activity_cancel` deferring a job's end to the slicing section. Not stated anywhere: every refusal while another plate slices; the wrong `alreadySliced`; the dropped `failure` texts; the gcode-file I/O hole; the nonexistent-plateId success of `print_dialog_open`; cancelled runs leaving no trace; superseded handles reading as `not_found`.

The live anomaly (sliced plate answered "refused", then `sliced: false`) sits here; its writer is unverified.
- `export_file`, `slice_inspect`, `slice_report` read the app-wide `is_background_process_slicing()` and refuse a valid plate while another plate slices.
- A cancelled run records nothing (`on_process_completed` keys on `event.error()`), so cancel, never sliced and "invalidated, cause unknown" collapse in the slicing section and in `activity_cancel`.
- A run start erases the plate's recorded failure (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:948-950); a cancelled retry therefore loses the reason the model had.

Cause (2), a filter drops the reason:
- `print_dialog_open` fills `failure` and drops it (confirmed (9)).
- `slice_report` with `valid: false` and no record does not say which of never / stale / running it is, although the snapshot has `estimateStatus`.
- `activity_cancel` uses one sentence for four endings of the tools' run, and `not_found` for a handle the tools issued and then superseded.
- `slicing.plates[].sliceFailure` is the short form (no `code`, `objectName`, `sequence`); only `slice_report` has the full one.
- `sliceWarnings` absent means both "none" and "never read while active" for a non-active plate.
- `slice_report` leaves a section out when the check could not run, same as when it was not asked.

Cause (3), fakes only produce imagined states: see the test section.

Cause (4), a generic error for a common, distinguishable state:
- `export_file`'s one `needs_step` sentence for never / stale / refused / failed / running (confirmed (4)).
- `slice_inspect`'s bare `{"valid": false}` for the same five (confirmed (7)).
- `slice_start`'s synthesized "The app did not start slicing this plate." whenever no Blocker is in the monitor.
- `export_file` presets: "the preset files exist" for any empty result (probable, unverified).

New cause (5), an I/O result is not checked: `slice_inspect` view gcode opens the file without `is_open()` and answers `valid: true, gcode: ""` (confirmed (7)).

New cause (6), the result is written before the work happens: `print_dialog_open` answers `opened: true` before its `CallAfter`; the deferred open can fail silently (`!m_installed`), show the person an error dialog (plate gone, including a plateId that was never in the project), or decline (`print_again` state moved), and no channel carries that back.

Stated in a description (plausibly intended): `busy` for a running slice and that nobody knows whose run it is; `export_file` needing a sliced plate; `slice_report` and `slice_inspect` saying "not sliced"; `slice_report` returning `valid: false` during a run (stated in `slice_start`'s text only); `print_dialog_open`'s `needs_step` and "opens after the call returns"; `activity_cancel` deferring a job's end to the slicing section. # Tool result inventory: slice, export, print and inspect tools

Read from the worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-silent-failures` at commit 5f3bd2e59a, code only; nothing was built or run. Paths are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Line numbers are from this commit.

Vocabulary: a "collapse" is two or more states the app can tell apart at the moment it answers, which the model receives as the same result. Causes are numbered as in the earlier analysis: (1) fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event; (2) a filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason; (3) tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined; (4) a generic error was used for a common, distinguishable state. Two new causes came up and are named where they apply: (5) an I/O result is not checked; (6) the result is written before the work happens.

Shared plumbing that every table relies on:

- `workspace_error_code()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:62-83) maps `WorkspaceError` kinds one to one onto codes: NotFound and InvalidId to `not_found`, StaleId and StaleSettings to `stale_workspace`, Busy to `busy`, NeedsStep to `needs_step`, Refused to `refused`, Failed to `failed`, WorkspaceUnavailable to `workspace_unavailable`, InvalidArgument to `invalid_arguments`, FeatureExpired to `feature_expired`. The message is the adapter's own text, so the collapses below are the adapter's, not the mapping's.
- `targets_sliced()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1054-1069) says whether every plate named (all plates when none is named) has `sliced == true`, and copies the first `slice_failure` it meets into `failure`. It starts from `sliced = !snapshot.plates.empty()`, so a plateId that matches no plate leaves `sliced` true.
- `WorkspacePlate::sliced` is `PartPlate::is_slice_result_valid()` read on every snapshot (Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1093); `slicing.running` is `Plater::is_background_process_slicing()`, which is the app-wide `p->m_is_slicing` flag (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:18402-18405). There is one slicing process for the whole app.
- `slice_failure` on a plate is the fork's own record (`m_slice_failures`), written by `record_slice_failure()` (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:977-1004) when OrcaSlicer calls the fork's `report_slice_declined()` hook or when a run ends with `event.error()`. The text comes from the print-issue monitor's first Blocker (`PrintIssues/PrintIssue.cpp:90-111`) or falls back to `"The app did not start slicing this plate."` (refused) or `"The slice stopped with an error."` (failed). The record is erased when the plate becomes sliced (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:935) and when a run starts on the current plate (948-950), and hidden from the snapshot while that plate is slicing (1115-1116).
- `report_slice_declined()` is called from three of OrcaSlicer's exits in `Plater::reslice()` and `Plater::start_next_slice()` (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:16070, 16116, 16262). Two other early returns in `reslice()` call nothing: the gizmo-in-editing-mode return (16076-16078) and the "could not stop UI job within 10000 ms" return (16082-16087). The "background process in idle state, use previous result" branch (16153-16165) also calls nothing; it sets the plate valid when it has printable instances and invalid when it has none.

Cause (1), fork reads leftover state instead of the event:
- `slice_start`'s `started` and `alreadySliced` are read from `slicing.running` and `is_slice_result_valid()` after the posted event returns. Two of OrcaSlicer's silent exits in `reslice()` (gizmo editing, UI job not stopped) and the idle branch have no `report_slice_declined()` hook, so they produce the generic refusal or a wrong `alreadySliced`. The live anomaly (sliced plate answered "refused", then `sliced: false`) sits here; its writer is unverified.
- `export_file`, `slice_inspect`, `slice_report` read the app-wide `is_background_process_slicing()` and refuse a valid plate while another plate slices.
- A cancelled run records nothing (`on_process_completed` keys on `event.error()`), so cancel, never sliced and "invalidated, cause unknown" collapse in the slicing section and in `activity_cancel`.
- A run start erases the plate's recorded failure (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:948-950); a cancelled retry therefore loses the reason the model had.

Cause (2), a filter drops the reason:
- `print_dialog_open` fills `failure` and drops it (confirmed (9)).
- `slice_report` with `valid: false` and no record does not say which of never / stale / running it is, although the snapshot has `estimateStatus`.
- `activity_cancel` uses one sentence for four endings of the tools' run, and `not_found` for a handle the tools issued and then superseded.
- `slicing.plates[].sliceFailure` is the short form (no `code`, `objectName`, `sequence`); only `slice_report` has the full one.
- `sliceWarnings` absent means both "none" and "never read while active" for a non-active plate.
- `slice_report` leaves a section out when the check could not run, same as when it was not asked.

Cause (3), fakes only produce imagined states: see the test section.

Cause (4), a generic error for a common, distinguishable state:
- `export_file`'s one `needs_step` sentence for never / stale / refused / failed / running (confirmed (4)).
- `slice_inspect`'s bare `{"valid": false}` for the same five (confirmed (7)).
- `slice_start`'s synthesized "The app did not start slicing this plate." whenever no Blocker is in the monitor.
- `export_file` presets: "the preset files exist" for any empty result (probable, unverified).

New cause (5), an I/O result is not checked: `slice_inspect` view gcode opens the file without `is_open()` and answers `valid: true, gcode: ""` (confirmed (7)).

New cause (6), the result is written before the work happens: `print_dialog_open` answers `opened: true` before its `CallAfter`; the deferred open can fail silently (`!m_installed`), show the person an error dialog (plate gone, including a plateId that was never in the project), or decline (`print_again` state moved), and no channel carries that back.

Stated in a description (plausibly intended): `busy` for a running slice and that nobody knows whose run it is; `export_file` needing a sliced plate; `slice_report` and `slice_inspect` saying "not sliced"; `slice_report` returning `valid: false` during a run (stated in `slice_start`'s text only); `print_dialog_open`'s `needs_step` and "opens after the call returns"; `activity_cancel` deferring a job's end to the slicing section. Not stated anywhere: every refusal while another plate slices; the wrong `alreadySliced`; the dropped `failure` texts; the gcode-file I/O hole; the nonexistent-plateId success of `print_dialog_open`; cancelled runs leaving no trace; superseded handles reading as `not_found`.

## Summary of collapses by cause

- (1) Reads Orca's leftover state instead of the event: printer_list excludes cloud-mode printers heard without a login, LAN printers without an access code, and (inferred) Moonraker hosts; printer_setup cannot tell a silent process `select_preset` failure.
- (2) A filter drops its reason: presets_list hides hidden presets and incompatible presets as `total 0`; every preset-naming tool reports a hidden preset as nonexistent (`unknown_preset`); settings_search answers `items: []` for a key in another scope, for `writable`/`changedOnly` filtering everything out, and for `changedOnly` on a preset not being edited; `unsupported_setting_mutation` merges Orca's read-only flag with the fork's blocked list; `selected` in presets_list means slot 1 only.
- (3) Fakes never produce the state: `FakeWorkspace` has no hidden presets and no device filtering; no search test for a cross-scope key.
- (4) One generic error for distinguishable states: calibration_generate's `failed` "The app did not generate the test"; presets_list and printer_list returning empty while presets or the device manager are not loaded; `workspace_unavailable` "No FFF process preset is selected" for a missing tab or a non-FFF printer; setup_record's "purpose must be one line." for a blank purpose; presets_list accepting a bad cursor as page one; a corrupt facts file reading as "no facts".
- (5) Throws, so no result at all: apply_settings when Orca will not open or save a preset; printer_setup when the facts file cannot be written or Orca will not select the previewed printer; settings_get on a preset missing a defined option.

Plausibly intended because the description states the limit: presets_list `compatibleOnly` default; alias versus name in every preset lookup; settings_search `writable` and `changedOnly` as filters (though not their silence); printer_setup_preview's "not installed… Add printer on Home" wording for a hidden printer preset. Everything else above is unstated.

# Tool result inventory: project, object, region, attachment, skill and picture tools

Read-only sweep of worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-silent-failures` at `5f3bd2e59a`. Paths below are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Nothing was built or run; every line is from reading code. Anything I did not trace end to end is marked **unverified**.

## Shared plumbing (applies to every tool)

| Where | What it does to results |
|---|---|
| `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp` | The only legal codes. `fail()` throws on any other (`Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2404-2407`). |
| `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:62-83` `workspace_error_code()` | `InvalidId`, `NotFound` -> `not_found`; `StaleId`, `StaleSettings` -> `stale_workspace`; `Busy` -> `busy`; `NeedsStep` -> `needs_step`; `Refused` -> `refused`; `Failed` -> `failed`; `WorkspaceUnavailable` -> `workspace_unavailable`; `InvalidArgument` -> `invalid_arguments`; `FeatureExpired` -> `feature_expired`. The adapter's message text passes through unchanged. So two adapter failures with the same kind and the same text are the same thing to the model; the inventory below is really an inventory of adapter message strings. |
| `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1733-1775` `validate_call()` | Any per-tool rule failure (`valid_arguments`) becomes `invalid_arguments` with `"The tool arguments do not match the registered contract."` plus only three generic additions: `" Not a parameter of this tool: <keys>."`, `" Missing: <keys>."`, `" <key> must be one of [...]"`. Rules that are not top-level (two sizing facets in object_place, both `plane` and `shells` in object_divide, a `scaleTo.sizeMm <= 0`, an `arrange.spacingMm > 100`) all collapse into the bare sentence. |
| `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1188-1193` | Every non-read-only tool fails `stale_workspace` (`"Nothing ran: the project changed after this call was made. ..."`) if the invalidating revision moved after submit. Details carry expected/current session and revision (`fail()`, 2410-2419). Distinguishable. |
| `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1086-1096, 1128-1130` | `local_save_failed` before (`"Nothing ran: the project could not be saved first. ..."`) or after (`"The change was made, but the project could not be saved. Do not repeat the call; ..."`) a versioned mutation. Distinguishable from each other and from the tool's own failures. |
| `Workspace/DialogListeners.cpp:57-92, 118-130` `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers` | A dialog that pops inside a scope is answered No > Cancel > OK > Yes (StepMeshDialog: OK) and recorded as an `OrcaMessage{title,text,buttons,answer,recognized,source}`. A dialog with none of the four buttons is cancelled with `recognized: false`. Only `DPIDialog::ShowModal` is intercepted (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_Utils.hpp:203-205`), and only while a scope is alive. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/NotificationManager.cpp:2969-2971, 3280`, `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI.cpp:252` | During a file load (`FileLoadScope`/`FileOpenScope` depth > 0), notifications become `OrcaMessage{source:"notification"}` and `show_error` becomes `source:"error"` with no buttons and `answer:""`. Outside a load (every other tool) `show_error` goes through `CallAfter` and shows the person an ErrorDialog after the tool has already returned; the tool result never carries it. |

---

## project_open

Registry: `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1082-1094`. Submit-time checks: `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:893-935`. Execution: `1253-1309`. Adapter: `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2539-2608`. Report: `Agent/ToolResults.cpp:486-560` (`load_report_result`), `386-408` (`orca_messages_result`).

| State the app can distinguish | Where distinguished | What the model receives today | Collapse? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` not absolute, or not a regular file | `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:899` | `invalid_arguments` "Give the absolute path of a file that exists." | no |
| `.3mf` with `unitConversion: inches` | `:903` | `invalid_arguments` "A project keeps its own units; inches applies to model files." | no |
| Projects store unreadable at lookup | `:910`, `:1272` | `local_save_failed` "Nothing was opened: JusPrin could not read its saved projects to check whether this file was opened before. Tell the person; ..." | no |
| File opened before, `openedBefore` absent; current project vs an earlier one; file changed / unchanged / unknown | `:912-928` | `opened_before` with "The open project, \"X\", was made from this file." or "\"X\" was made from this file before." + " The file has changed since." / " The file has not changed since." / nothing; details `{project, current, fileChanged}` | no |

| Release of the open project cancelled (autosave hook returned `wxID_CANCEL`) | `:2589` after `release_project` `:2598` | `failed` "The open project could not be saved, so it stays open" + `report` | no (coordinator also has its own `local_save_failed`; two codes for one family, but both are clear) |

# Reproduce tool results over MCP with no model: shell harness --manual-mcp plus tests/mcp/probe.py.
import json, os, subprocess, sys, time, shutil
from urllib.parse import urlsplit
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "tests/mcp"))
import probe

worktree, out_dir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
fixture = os.path.join(out_dir, "fixture"); home = os.path.join(out_dir, "home")
shutil.rmtree(fixture, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(fixture); os.makedirs(home, exist_ok=True)
exe = os.path.join(worktree, "build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness")
log = open(os.path.join(out_dir, "harness.log"), "w")
proc = subprocess.Popen([exe, "--manual-mcp", fixture], env={**os.environ, "HOME": home}, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
try:
    for _ in range(120):
        time.sleep(1)
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(fixture, "jusprin", "mcp.json")) and "FIXTURE READY" in open(log.name).read():
            break
    else:
        raise SystemExit("harness not ready")
    url = json.load(open(os.path.join(fixture, "jusprin", "mcp.json")))
    url = url.get("url") or url.get("endpoint") or next(v for v in url.values() if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("http"))
    ep = urlsplit(url)
    results = []
    def call(name, args):
        r = probe.call(ep, "tools/call", {"name": name, "arguments": args})
        text = r if isinstance(r, str) else json.dumps(r)
        print(f"\n### {name} {json.dumps(args)}\n{text[:3000]}")
        results.append({"tool": name, "arguments": args, "result": r})
        return r
    def content(r):
        try:
            c = r["result"]["content"][0]["text"]
            return json.loads(c)
        except Exception:
            return r
    ws = content(call("workspace_inspect", {}))
    plates = ws.get("plates", {}).get("items", []) if isinstance(ws, dict) else []
    session = ws.get("sessionId") if isinstance(ws, dict) else None
    unsliced = next((p["plateId"] for p in plates if not p.get("sliced")), None)
    sliced = next((p["plateId"] for p in plates if p.get("sliced")), None)
    print("\nplates:", plates, "unsliced:", unsliced, "sliced:", sliced)
    gcode_path = os.path.join(out_dir, "out.gcode")
    # Findings 7, 8, 4, 9 on the never-sliced plate.
    call("slice_report", {"plateId": unsliced})
    call("slice_inspect", {"plateId": unsliced, "view": "layers"})
    call("export_file", {"sessionId": session, "kind": "gcode", "path": gcode_path, "plateId": unsliced, "overwrite": True})
    call("print_dialog_open", {"plateId": unsliced})
    # The same four while that plate slices.
    call("slice_start", {"plateId": unsliced})
    call("slice_report", {"plateId": unsliced})
    call("slice_inspect", {"plateId": unsliced, "view": "layers"})
    call("export_file", {"sessionId": session, "kind": "gcode", "path": gcode_path, "plateId": unsliced, "overwrite": True})
    call("print_dialog_open", {"plateId": unsliced})
    # And the sliced plate while the other slices (the app-wide flag).
    if sliced:
        call("slice_report", {"plateId": sliced})
    time.sleep(8)
    call("workspace_inspect", {"sections": ["slicing"]})
    # Finding 11: a key in another scope.
    call("settings_search", {"scope": "printer", "query": "sparse_infill_density"})
    call("settings_get", {"scope": "printer", "keys": ["sparse_infill_density"]})
    # Finding 10: an installed but hidden filament against a nonexistent one.
    call("presets_list", {"kind": "filament", "query": "PETG HF"})
    call("presets_list", {"kind": "filament", "query": "PETG HF", "compatibleOnly": False})
    call("presets_list", {"kind": "filament", "query": "No Such Filament Zzz"})
    call("settings_get", {"scope": "filament", "target": {"preset": "Bambu PETG HF @BBL X1C"}, "keys": ["nozzle_temperature"]})
    call("settings_get", {"scope": "filament", "target": {"preset": "No Such Filament Zzz"}, "keys": ["nozzle_temperature"]})
    json.dump(results, open(os.path.join(out_dir, "results.json"), "w"), indent=1)
finally:
    proc.terminate()
    try: proc.wait(20)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: proc.kill()
    print("\nharness exit", proc.returncode)
    hidden = os.path.join(fixture, "system", "BBL", "filament", "Bambu PETG HF @BBL X1C.json")
    print("installed system profile for the hidden preset exists:", os.path.exists(hidden), hidden)
EOF

## What the tests and fakes cover

- `tests/jusprin_support/FakeWorkspace.hpp`: `render_view` (`:386-394`) always returns a fixed PNG; `import_objects` (`:334-382`) always adds one object and never fails after the file check; `open_project` (`:1235-1261`) always succeeds past the path check; `analyze_object` (`:896-914`) returns scripted sections; `region_status` (`:623-644`) reads `binding_lost`/`artifacts_missing` from test-set maps. None of the fakes produces: a blank render, a load Orca refused silently, a direction with no facets, a `partList` over 16, a convert_unit that did nothing, or an arrange that failed with a reason.
- `tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp`: cases at `:372, :400, :1032, :1408, :1463, :1490, :1535, :1829, :1945, :2214` exercise the happy paths and the argument/id failures. A grep for the adapter strings "rendered nothing", "did not open", "did not import", "not a face", "No facet", "cannot merge", "could not repair", "produced nothing", "did not split", "did not merge" finds none of them asserted. So every collapse above tagged cause (1) or (4) is also cause (3): the tests only know the states the fake can make.

## Collapses, grouped by cause

**(1) Fork reads Orca's leftover state instead of the event**
- view_render: blank PNG for empty/non-printable/off-plate/FBO-failed/no-shader renders (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:159-162`). Not stated.
- object_place `unitsFix`: `model.objects.size() - 1` assumed to be the converted object (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1816`); the dialog answers inside `convert_unit` are discarded (`:1814`). Not stated. Wrong-id part **unverified**.
- object_divide shells: `added = 1` when Orca split nothing, `pieces` names the last object (`OrcaReshape.cpp:245-248`); Orca's warning dialog shows to the person. Not stated. **unverified** reachability.
- object_divide plane that crosses the box but not the mesh: one-piece "success" with a new id. **unverified**.
- object_merge: "The app cannot merge these objects" when the real cause is an unregistered selection (`OrcaReshape.cpp:303-304`). Not stated.
- plate_layout arrange: `notPlaced` recomputed from geometry while Orca's own "ignored the following objects" notification and "Arrange failed" error go to the person (`ArrangeJob.cpp:615, 712`; `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1562-1572`).
- project_delete_items: a dialog Orca raised mid-delete is logged, not returned (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2874-2876`).

**(2) A filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason**
- object_analyze `mesh.partList` capped at 16 with no flag (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1919`). Not stated.
- object_analyze features: a plane with a non-finite centre dropped silently (`:1972`). Not stated.
- object_analyze fit: overlaps checked for the first instance's plate only (`:2080-2098`). Not stated.
- object_analyze regions: `bindingLost` never computed for box/cylinder/direction/object (`OrcaRegions.cpp:408-409`); a record whose object cannot be matched shows as both flags true and no `objectId` (`:398`). Not stated.
- object_analyze measure: `measurement: {}` with no word on why (`:2136-2142`). Not stated.
- region_annotate: a box/cylinder volume that touches nothing is a success (`OrcaRegions.cpp` no check). Not stated.
- project_open `settingsOutcome: "geometry_only"` merges the file's choice, Orca's choice and the caller's `keep` (`ToolResults.cpp:538-541`). Plausibly intended.
- project_attachment_read: refused folders and traversal read as "no attachment" (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:180-189`). Plausibly intended.
- plate_layout: no-op rows look like applied rows; multi-plate copies all moved by one delta (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1705`). First plausibly intended, second not stated.
- project_delete_items: plate deletion's destination plate only inferable (`:2868`). Stated in the description.
- jobs `failed` drops the exception text (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1518`). Not stated.

**(3) Tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined**
- Every item above; see "What the tests and fakes cover". The fake's `render_view` is the clearest instance: it cannot draw an empty plate.

**(4) A generic error for a state that is common and distinguishable**
- `validate_call`'s bare "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract." for object_place facet conflicts and object_divide plane/shells conflicts (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1740`, rules `:289-351`). Not stated beyond the description prose.
- "\"<h>\" is not a face of this object" / "is not a feature of this object" / "is not a feature of <name>" for five structurally different handle problems, hole-for-face included (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1775-1788, 2114-2125, 2028`; `OrcaRegions.cpp:163-172`). Not stated.
- region_annotate "No facet of <name> matches that face any more" with code `stale_workspace` for a *direction* nothing points to (`OrcaRegions.cpp:271-275`). Not stated; the code sends the model down the wrong path.
- project_open / imports "The app did not open that file" / "The app did not import that file" when Orca was silent (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2591, 2766`). The reason rides in `report.messages` only when Orca spoke. Partly stated ("The app shows no dialogs while it loads: each one is answered ... and returned in report.messages").
- object_import "The model file does not exist" for an empty file (`:2733`).
- object_place `scaleTo` zero-extent failure after a units fix already ran (`:1826`); project_delete_items region removal failing after deletions (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1497-1500`); region_annotate apply failing after removals (`OrcaRegions.cpp:358-359`): three late failures whose message does not say what already changed. All rare.
- project_attachment_read "The app could not read that picture" for corrupt vs too-large-after-re-encode (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:211`).

**New cause worth naming: (5) a dialog outside any `ScopedLeastChangeAnswers` scope**
- `divide_object` shells path runs Orca's `split_object`, which can show "The selected object couldn't be split." (`Plater.cpp:7684`) and "Disable Auto-Drop to preserve Z positioning?" (`:7705`) to the person while the tool is running, with no record in the result. `show_error` calls outside loads (`GUI.cpp:252-258`) are deferred by `CallAfter` and reach the person after the tool returned. **(1) Fork reads Orca's leftover state instead of the event**

- object_divide plane that crosses the box but not the mesh: one-piece "success" with a new id. **unverified**.

- plate_layout arrange: `notPlaced` recomputed from geometry while Orca's own "ignored the following objects" notification and "Arrange failed" error go to the person (`ArrangeJob.cpp:615, 712`; `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1562-1572`).

**(2) A filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason**

- object_analyze features: a plane with a non-finite centre dropped silently (`:1972`). Not stated.
- object_analyze fit: overlaps checked for the first instance's plate only (`:2080-2098`). Not stated.

- project_attachment_read: refused folders and traversal read as "no attachment" (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:180-189`). Plausibly intended.

**(3) Tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined**

**(4) A generic error for a state that is common and distinguishable**

cat > agent-docs/jusprin/tool-result-inventory.md <<'EOF'
# Tool result inventory: what the app can tell apart, and what the model reads

Written 2026-11-01, from the code at `5f3bd2e59a` (`jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4` plus the Bambu connection fix). It answers one question for every tool the model can call:

**Does every state the app can tell apart at the moment it answers map to a result the model can tell apart?**

Where two states the app distinguishes produce the same result (the same code and message, an empty list, a bare `valid: false`, or a success that says nothing), the row is a **collapse**. The rule these rows are held to is in the tool guide, ["A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result"](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#a-reason-travels-with-every-refusal-and-every-empty-result), and in the header of `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`.

## How to use this document

- **Adding or changing a tool:** list its states here first, one row each, and say what the result carries for each. A tool is not done while a row collapses. The guard for a tool is a state table test that arranges each row and asserts the results differ (`tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp` under the `[states]` tag, `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", and the `--printer-setup` harness checks named `*_are_told_apart`).
- **Reading a row:** "Where" is the code that distinguishes the state at `5f3bd2e59a` (paths under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`). "Result" quotes what the model reads. "Cause" is one of the numbered causes below. "Status" says whether the collapse is open, fixed, or accepted.
- **Reproduction before a fix:** a collapse is fixed only once it has been reproduced in the real app or the real harness. The status column says how each one was. Kenneth's rule: no fix for a failure not reproduced; a fake taught to fail is not a reproduction on its own.

## Why these collapses exist: the causes

The tool guide governs what the model is told and how a tool is shaped. These collapses are on the app's side, in the code that reads OrcaSlicer's state and turns it into a result. Six causes account for every row below; the first four were named before this inventory, the last two were found while writing it.

1. **Fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event that happened.** `OrcaPrinterBackend` reported a failed Bambu connection as "The selected printer changed" because upstream's handler clears the selection on failure; the slice tools read the app-wide "is slicing" flag instead of which plate's run it is.
2. **A filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason.** Connection candidates of another model, hidden presets, a key that belongs to another scope: the loop that drops them keeps no record, and the model reads an empty list.
3. **Tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined.** The Bambu fake never sent `ConnectStatusFailed`; the harness check for a failed connection simulated a selection change instead; the fake workspace has no hidden presets, no empty render, no refused host.
4. **A generic error was used for states that are common and that the app distinguishes.** Kenneth's 2026-10-15 rule gives one generic error to failures that are rare and that the app cannot tell apart. Applied to never sliced, refused, failed and slicing now, which the snapshot tells apart, it became cause 4.
5. **A result is written before the work happens, or without checking the work's outcome.** `print_dialog_open` answers `opened: true` before its deferred open; `slice_inspect` reads a G-code file without checking that it opened.
6. **A dialog or a throw outside any channel.** OrcaSlicer shows the person a dialog in the middle of a tool call that no scope answers, or a handler throws and the activity never gets a result at all.

## The sweep's eleven findings and where they stand

| # | Tool(s) | Collapse | Cause | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `printer_connect` outcome note | A Bambu connection refused by the plug-in read "The selected printer changed" (any code, or the connection lost) or "The printer is no longer available" (code 5, a wrong access code) | 1, 3 | open at `5f3bd2e59a` |
| 2 | `printer_connect` outcome note | A Moonraker or OctoPrint test that answered 401, or answered as another kind of service, read "Could not reach the print host" | 1, 4 | open |
| 3 | `printer_connection_status`, `printer_connect`, the search's notes | A heard printer of another model, of this model but linked to another saved printer, or of this model while this printer is linked to another device, was dropped and the model read "found no printer of this model" | 2, 3 | open |
| 4 | `export_file` | One `needs_step` sentence for never sliced, stale, refused, failed and slicing now | 1, 4 | open |
| 5 | `printer_list` | A cloud-mode printer heard on the network with nobody signed in, or a LAN printer without an access code, is absent with no reason | 1, 3 | open |
| 6 | the Add chat's "On the network now" line | Read once when the panel opens from the account-or-LAN list: too many (account printers anywhere), too few (announcing printers without a code), or omitted | 2 | open |
| 7 | `slice_inspect` | A bare `valid: false` for the same five states; a G-code file that does not open reads as an empty file | 4, 5 | open |
| 8 | `slice_report` | A bare `valid: false` for never sliced, stale and slicing now; a valid plate reads `valid: false` while another plate slices | 1, 2 | open |
| 9 | `print_dialog_open` | The slice failure it looked up is dropped; a plate id that is not in the project is answered `opened: true` | 2, 5 | open |
| 10 | `presets_list`, every tool naming a preset | An installed but hidden preset reads as one that does not exist (`total: 0`, `unknown_preset` "No ... preset is named") | 2, 3 | open |
| 11 | `settings_search` | A key that is a setting of another scope gives `items: []`, identical to a key no scope has | 2, 3 | open |

## Printer chat tools (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`)

Five tools, offered only in the printer panel. Their backend is `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp`; the tests' fake is `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp`.

### printer_identify

| State | Where | Result | Collapse |
|---|---|---|---|
| A catalogue id not on the list | `PrinterConversation.cpp` `identify` | `unknown_printer` "\"X\" is not on the printer list; copy it exactly from the printer list." | no |
| More than three candidates | same | `too_many` "More than three fit. Ask one question that narrows it down instead." | no |
| A nozzle the model does not ship | `unknown_nozzle` | `unknown_nozzle` with the sizes it ships | no |
| Success | | `printers[]` with assumed nozzle, plate and filament, and `alreadyYours` | no |

### printer_add

| State | Where | Result | Collapse |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unknown catalogue id; unshipped nozzle | `add` | `unknown_printer`, `unknown_nozzle` | no |
| The same printer added twice in one conversation | `m_added` | `already_added` naming the saved printer | no |
| The backend refused the save (profile install failed, name clash) | `add_failed` | `add_failed` with the backend's sentence for the person | no |
| Success | | `printer` as saved | no |

### printer_change

| State | Where | Result | Collapse |
|---|---|---|---|
| No nozzle named; the same nozzle as now; an unshipped nozzle | `change` | `nothing_to_change` (two sentences), `unknown_nozzle` | no |
| The backend refused the change | | `change_failed` with the backend's sentence; `discarded` lists dropped unsaved edits | no |
| Success | | `changed[]`, `discarded[]`, `printer` | no |

### printer_connection_status

| State | Where | Result | Collapse |
|---|---|---|---|
| No saved printer in this conversation | `connection_status` | `no_printer` | no |
| Bambu Lab printer without the network plug-in | `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection` | `state: unavailable`, `message` naming the plug-in, the notice card drawn once | no |
| Bambu Lab, plug-in loaded, device manager or agent missing | same | `unavailable` "Connecting is not available right now." | minor: two causes, one sentence; both rare |
| Print host: no address saved; address saved, never tested; connection type "other" | same | `not_configured`; `unknown` "A connection is saved. Test it..."; `unavailable` "Configure this connection type in Printer settings." | no |
| Print host: a test attempt waiting, verified, failed; settings changed since verified | `settle`, `m_host_attempt` | `connecting`, `verified`, `failed` + message; "Connection settings changed. Test the new connection again." | see finding 2 for the failed message |
| Bambu: a printer in LAN mode of this model, offered | candidate loop `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:481-492` | `candidates[]` {deviceId, name, address} | no |
| Bambu: a printer in cloud mode on this network | same loop; `connection_json` | `seen[]` with `reason: cloud_mode` | no (fixed on this branch's base, `ff2fee4fbd`) |
| Bambu: a printer on the account not heard on this network | same | `seen[]` with `reason: account_only` | no |
| Bambu: a heard printer of another model | loop line 482 `continue` | dropped; `candidates: []`, `seen: []` | **finding 3**, cause 2 |
| Bambu: a heard printer of this model, this saved printer linked to a different device | line 484 | dropped | **finding 3** |
| Bambu: a heard printer of this model already linked to another saved printer | lines 486-489 | dropped | **finding 3** |
| Bambu: a heard printer in LAN mode whose `bind_state` is not `free` | line 489 `is_avaliable()` | dropped | **finding 3**, unverified whether a LAN-mode printer reports `occupied` |
| Search not started; started; listening with none after 15 s; port taken; not listening | `search_json` | `search.state`, `secondsAgo` | no (fixed on this branch's base, `ff10faa501`) |
| Connected: fresh push data; verified before, silent now; never connected | `communicating`, `configured` | `verified`, `unknown`, `not_configured` | no |
| Connecting: a connection attempt waiting | `m_connection_attempt` | `connecting` | no |
| Connecting, then the plug-in reports `ConnectStatusFailed` with code 5 (upstream erases the saved code) | `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:2092-2105` acts; the backend reads only `get_my_machine == nullptr` | `failed` "The printer is no longer available. Refresh the printer list and try again." | **finding 1**, cause 1 |
| Connecting, then `ConnectStatusFailed` with any other code, or `ConnectStatusLost` | handler clears the selection; backend reads the selection | `failed` "The selected printer changed. Select this printer again to reconnect." | **finding 1** |

# Tool result inventory: what the app can tell apart, and what the model reads

Written 2026-11-01, from the code at `5f3bd2e59a` (`jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4` plus the Bambu connection fix). It answers one question for every tool the model can call:

**Does every state the app can tell apart at the moment it answers map to a result the model can tell apart?**

Where two states the app distinguishes produce the same result (the same code and message, an empty list, a bare `valid: false`, or a success that says nothing), the row is a **collapse**. The rule these rows are held to is in the tool guide, ["A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result"](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#a-reason-travels-with-every-refusal-and-every-empty-result), and in the header of `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`.

## How to use this document

- **Adding or changing a tool:** list its states here first, one row each, and say what the result carries for each. A tool is not done while a row collapses. The guard for a tool is a state table test that arranges each row and asserts the results differ (`tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp` under the `[states]` tag, `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", and the `--printer-setup` harness checks named `*_are_told_apart`).
- **Reading a row:** "Where" is the code that distinguishes the state at `5f3bd2e59a` (paths under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`). "Result" quotes what the model reads. "Cause" is one of the numbered causes below. "Status" says whether the collapse is open, fixed, or accepted.
- **Reproduction before a fix:** a collapse is fixed only once it has been reproduced in the real app or the real harness. The status column says how each one was. Kenneth's rule: no fix for a failure not reproduced; a fake taught to fail is not a reproduction on its own.

## Why these collapses exist: the causes

The tool guide governs what the model is told and how a tool is shaped. These collapses are on the app's side, in the code that reads OrcaSlicer's state and turns it into a result. Six causes account for every row below; the first four were named before this inventory, the last two were found while writing it.

1. **Fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event that happened.** `OrcaPrinterBackend` reported a failed Bambu connection as "The selected printer changed" because upstream's handler clears the selection on failure; the slice tools read the app-wide "is slicing" flag instead of which plate's run it is.
2. **A filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason.** Connection candidates of another model, hidden presets, a key that belongs to another scope: the loop that drops them keeps no record, and the model reads an empty list.
3. **Tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined.** The Bambu fake never sent `ConnectStatusFailed`; the harness check for a failed connection simulated a selection change instead; the fake workspace has no hidden presets, no empty render, no refused host.
4. **A generic error was used for states that are common and that the app distinguishes.** Kenneth's 2026-10-15 rule gives one generic error to failures that are rare and that the app cannot tell apart. Applied to never sliced, refused, failed and slicing now, which the snapshot tells apart, it became cause 4.
5. **A result is written before the work happens, or without checking the work's outcome.** `print_dialog_open` answers `opened: true` before its deferred open; `slice_inspect` reads a G-code file without checking that it opened.
6. **A dialog or a throw outside any channel.** OrcaSlicer shows the person a dialog in the middle of a tool call that no scope answers, or a handler throws and the activity never gets a result at all.

+# Tool result inventory: what the app can tell apart, and what the model reads
+Written 2026-11-01, from the code at `5f3bd2e59a` (`jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4` plus the Bambu connection fix). It answers one question for every tool the model can call:
+**Does every state the app can tell apart at the moment it answers map to a result the model can tell apart?**

+Where two states the app distinguishes produce the same result (the same code and message, an empty list, a bare `valid: false`, or a success that says nothing), the row is a **collapse**. The rule these rows are held to is in the tool guide, ["A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result"](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#a-reason-travels-with-every-refusal-and-every-empty-result), and in the header of `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`.

+- **Adding or changing a tool:** list its states here first, one row each, and say what the result carries for each. A tool is not done while a row collapses. The guard for a tool is a state table test that arranges each row and asserts the results differ (`tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp` under the `[states]` tag, `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", and the `--printer-setup` harness checks named `*_are_told_apart`).

+- **Reading a row:** "Where" is the code that distinguishes the state at `5f3bd2e59a` (paths under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`). "Result" quotes what the model reads. "Cause" is one of the numbered causes below. "Status" says whether the collapse is open, fixed, or accepted.

+- **Reproduction before a fix:** a collapse is fixed only once it has been reproduced in the real app or the real harness. The status column says how each one was. Kenneth's rule: no fix for a failure not reproduced; a fake taught to fail is not a reproduction on its own.
+## Why these collapses exist: the causes

+The tool guide governs what the model is told and how a tool is shaped. These collapses are on the app's side, in the code that reads OrcaSlicer's state and turns it into a result. Six causes account for every row below; the first four were named before this inventory, the last two were found while writing it.

+1. **Fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event that happened.** `OrcaPrinterBackend` reported a failed Bambu connection as "The selected printer changed" because upstream's handler clears the selection on failure; the slice tools read the app-wide "is slicing" flag instead of which plate's run it is.

+2. **A filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason.** Connection candidates of another model, hidden presets, a key that belongs to another scope: the loop that drops them keeps no record, and the model reads an empty list.

+3. **Tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined.** The Bambu fake never sent `ConnectStatusFailed`; the harness check for a failed connection simulated a selection change instead; the fake workspace has no hidden presets, no empty render, no refused host.

+4. **A generic error was used for states that are common and that the app distinguishes.** Kenneth's 2026-10-15 rule gives one generic error to failures that are rare and that the app cannot tell apart. Applied to never sliced, refused, failed and slicing now, which the snapshot tells apart, it became cause 4.

+5. **A result is written before the work happens, or without checking the work's outcome.** `print_dialog_open` answers `opened: true` before its deferred open; `slice_inspect` reads a G-code file without checking that it opened.

+6. **A dialog or a throw outside any channel.** OrcaSlicer shows the person a dialog in the middle of a tool call that no scope answers, or a handler throws and the activity never gets a result at all.

# Tool result inventory: what the app can tell apart, and what the model reads

Written 2026-11-01, from the code at `5f3bd2e59a` (`jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4` plus the Bambu connection fix). It answers one question for every tool the model can call:

**Does every state the app can tell apart at the moment it answers map to a result the model can tell apart?**

Where two states the app distinguishes produce the same result (the same code and message, an empty list, a bare `valid: false`, or a success that says nothing), the row is a **collapse**. The rule these rows are held to is in the tool guide, ["A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result"](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#a-reason-travels-with-every-refusal-and-every-empty-result), and in the header of `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`.

## How to use this document

- **Adding or changing a tool:** list its states here first, one row each, and say what the result carries for each. A tool is not done while a row collapses. The guard for a tool is a state table test that arranges each row and asserts the results differ (`tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp` under the `[states]` tag, `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", and the `--printer-setup` harness checks named `*_are_told_apart`).
- **Reading a row:** "Where" is the code that distinguishes the state at `5f3bd2e59a` (paths under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`). "Result" quotes what the model reads. "Cause" is one of the numbered causes below. "Status" says whether the collapse is open, fixed, or accepted.
- **Reproduction before a fix:** a collapse is fixed only once it has been reproduced in the real app or the real harness. The status column says how each one was. Kenneth's rule: no fix for a failure not reproduced; a fake taught to fail is not a reproduction on its own.

## Why these collapses exist: the causes

The tool guide governs what the model is told and how a tool is shaped. These collapses are on the app's side, in the code that reads OrcaSlicer's state and turns it into a result. Six causes account for every row below; the first four were named before this inventory, the last two were found while writing it.

1. **Fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event that happened.** `OrcaPrinterBackend` reported a failed Bambu connection as "The selected printer changed" because upstream's handler clears the selection on failure; the slice tools read the app-wide "is slicing" flag instead of which plate's run it is.
2. **A filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason.** Connection candidates of another model, hidden presets, a key that belongs to another scope: the loop that drops them keeps no record, and the model reads an empty list.
3. **Tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined.** The Bambu fake never sent `ConnectStatusFailed`; the harness check for a failed connection simulated a selection change instead; the fake workspace has no hidden presets, no empty render, no refused host.
4. **A generic error was used for states that are common and that the app distinguishes.** Kenneth's 2026-10-15 rule gives one generic error to failures that are rare and that the app cannot tell apart. Applied to never sliced, refused, failed and slicing now, which the snapshot tells apart, it became cause 4.
5. **A result is written before the work happens, or without checking the work's outcome.** `print_dialog_open` answers `opened: true` before its deferred open; `slice_inspect` reads a G-code file without checking that it opened.
6. **A dialog or a throw outside any channel.** OrcaSlicer shows the person a dialog in the middle of a tool call that no scope answers, or a handler throws and the activity never gets a result at all.
